[LREG.4.7] **A capture is a function of the matched fact and the pattern
alone, so how many times an implementation evaluates it is not observable.** An
engine **may** compute a capture once and carry the result, or re-derive it
wherever the value is used, or both in one artefact. No program can tell the
difference, so this document does not choose.

**This is why the clause is about purity and not about caching.** It is the
same rule [RDSC.5a.1a] applies to aggregation reads, run in the opposite
direction: there, a read **must not** mutate state, *because* the number of reads
is unfixed under any evaluation strategy and a non-idempotent read would make
the answer depend on how many rules referenced it. Here the idempotence is free —
RE2 is deterministic and the fact is immutable while matched — and what it buys
back is the engine's choice.

**What that choice costs is worth knowing before it surprises someone.** The
single-pattern case is free: the test and the fire happen in one pass, so the
match is already in hand. A join is where re-derivation is reached, because the
capture is needed when the *other* side arrives, and it is paid per candidate
fact examined rather than once per join — a constant factor on work the join
already does, not a new complexity class. An engine that carries the value
instead pays storage rather than time. Both conform.

**Under `realtime` the cost lands where the contract already accounts for it.**
Re-matching is bounded because RE2 is linear by construction ([LREG.7.1]) — it is
the reason that engine is mandated rather than a convenience — so the work is
pump work under `pump_wcet_ns` ([RTCT.7.1]) rather than an unbounded
allocation. An engine that carries the value instead consumes the intern table,
which `intern_cap` and `intern_bytes_cap` already bound. Neither strategy needs
a cap that does not exist.
